Abnorm lyte, ETOH use or w/draw?

Meds that ↓sz threshold: TCA, wellbutrin, opioids, antipsych, fluoroquinolones, penicillins, carbapenems, stimulants, anesthetics (lidocaine)

Incont: intra-oral lacerations (gen, tonic-clonic)
post ictal period (time to return to baseline awareness/funct)? Behavior?: typical Sx/S or duration?
2/2 trauma or inj: ex. Inj during sz, inj precipitating sz
Musc tone (loss of)
ROS
tumor   -    infect    -    hydrocephalus   -    meds    -    trauma
Eti
: VITAMINS
Vasc: CVAs, bleeds
Infectious: meningitis, encephalitis, brain abscess
traumatic/toxic: head inj, penetrating trauma (GSW), EtOH, cocaine -focal irritate
Autoimmune: CNS vasculitis, lupus
Met (esp for 1st time): lytes, glucose, hyperthyroid, hepatic or uremic encephalopathy
Idiopathic: Epilepsy
Neoplasm: irritate, struct chgs
Syncope, Psychogenic, other ddx
Sz types
focal w retained or impaired awareness (simple focal)                                         Post-ictal period: shorter
MC Location: 1 part of motor cortex                    **extent of motor cortex involved = severity**
Severity: aura -to- gen (simple focal sz Sx)
Gen tonic-clonic (grand mal or major motor)                                             Post-ictal period: longer
Sx/S: LOC & musc tone -> rhythmic overall musc contract
Fall out of bed/chair, tongue biting, incont
red flags: 1st sz   -   prolonged post-ictal state    -  incomplete recovery of neuro deficits    -   2ndry inj
todd's paralysis:
brief, transient paralysis following a sz
status epilepticus:
life threatening: hypoxia & autonomic instability
single/back-to-back tonic clonic -persist for 5min OR successive seizures w/o return to baseline alertness
tx: IV benzos (rectal if ⍉IV access & pt actively seizing), airway support, antiseizure meds
**********Only red flags to hsp**********
Other HPI

assoc manifestations                -    Location                                      -     meds             -    efforts to tx
Gait
HPI:    -      assoc dx: arthritis, CVA, sz     -   new meds?    -    falling, balance   -    gait chg: ortho/neuro/both?
Tremor
HPI              upper vs lower extremities? Both?                    -    onset: sudden or gradual                     -     meds
character: worse w rest, intentional mvt          -    relieved by: rest, activity, EToH       -    assoc problems
Assoc Dx: Hyperthyroidism      -    familial tremor      -    liver or kidney dx      -    ETOH use      -     MS
assoc meds:     neuroleptics (antipsych)                -   valproate, phenytoin          -    caffeine
Albuterol     -   corticosteroids      -    pseudoephedrine              -     antiarrhythmias
types of tremors
Resting tremor: present @ rest, ↓w voluntary mvt (4–6 Hz)
Eti: Parkinson’s dz (MCC), drug-induced parkinsonism (neuroleptics, metoclopramide), Wilson’s dz
Intention (action) tremor: worsens as limb approaches a target; ⍉@ rest
Eti: cerebellar dz or damage (MS, cerebellar CVA, chronic ETOH, spinocerebellar ataxias), phenytoin or valproate toxicity
Essential/postural tremor: occurs w sustained posture or action; relieved by rest or sm amount of ETOH
Eti: essential (familial) tremor (MCC of action tremor), hyperthyroidism, meds (albuterol, corticosteroids, caffeine, pseudoephedrine, valproate, lithium), anxiety, physio (exertion, caffeine)
Asterixis (“liver flap”): hand-flapping tremor on wrist dorsiflexion; ⍉a true tremor
Eti: met encephalopathy (hepatic, uremic, CO2 retention), toxic/med Eti

HPI              location: prox/dist/symmetric/asym                        -       onset
character: gen/localized                                                      -     Meds: HIV anti-virals, amphotericin B
concurrent chronic illness: HIV, nutritional or ↓B12                   -    Weakness vs fatigue? Both?
Acute weakness or numbness suggests: vasc event (CVA vs TIA)      -     assoc Sx/S

Dizziness

Positional?

loss of funct    -   fever    -   wake pt from sleep    -   unremitting   -   Hx CA w poss met potential to brain
Red Flags:

sudden loss of funct
Eti:  vasc event   -  CNS/PNS trauma    -  intoxication    -  drug OD   -    drug: side effect, toxicity, w/draw, 5HT syndrome
loss or sudden Δ in LOC
Eti:       sz      -    Trauma      -   delirium      -  ↓BG      -   drug OD      -   IC process: CVA, tumor, trauma, bleed
cerebral hypoperfusion: dysrhythmia, brady, hypovolemia, orthostasis, AS
Anatomy
Brain Bleed
Brain blood supply = 20% CO
arterial supply: 2 internal carotids & 2 vertebral
venous drainage: venous plexuses + dural sinuses & 2 internal jugular veins
places blood can accumulate: epidural space     -     subdural space     -     subarachnoid space
Comp of brain bleed: ischemia -relieve P by burr hole
acute weakness or numbness suggests: vasc event (CVA vs TIA)
